title: Join Orders with Customer Details
description:
Write a query to return each order with its customer's details. Return `order_id` (from orders.id), `customer_name`, `city`, `amount`, and `order_date`.

**Table: customers** — `id`, `name`, `city`

**Table: orders** — `id`, `customer_id`, `amount`, `order_date`
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE customers (id INT, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR); CREATE TABLE orders (id INT, customer_id INT, amount DECIMAL, order_date DATE); INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1,'Alice Johnson','New York'),(2,'Bob Smith','Chicago'),(3,'Carol Davis','Houston'),(4,'Diana Prince','Seattle'); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (1,1,150.00,'2026-09-01'),(2,2,200.00,'2026-09-05'),(3,1,75.00,'2026-09-10'),(4,3,320.00,'2026-09-12'),(5,2,125.00,'2026-09-15'),(6,4,450.00,'2026-09-18');
solution_sql: SELECT o.id AS order_id, c.name AS customer_name, c.city, o.amount, o.order_date FROM orders o INNER JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id

test_cases.description: Returns 6 rows with order details enriched by customer name and city

hints: `INNER JOIN table ON condition` returns only rows where the join condition matches in both tables.
The join key is `orders.customer_id = customers.id`. All 6 orders have a matching customer, so all 6 are returned.
explanation: `INNER JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.id` links each order to its customer. Since every order has a valid `customer_id`, all 6 order rows are included with the enriched customer name and city.
